subject: Customer keys & egress authorization for private deployment
messages:
From: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@catalysthealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Customer keys & egress authorization for private deployment

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Catalyst Health is preparing the procurement package for a Private (VPC + on-prem) deployment and Legal/Procurement asked for a concise written response on three items before we proceed to redlines: 

1) Key custody model — we need confirmation that customer-managed keys (BYOK) are supported for the private control plane and that Redwood operators will not have access to plaintext keys or secrets. If there are operator break-glass procedures, please describe the preconditions and audit trail.

2) Egress and telemetry — our security team needs assurance that no customer PII or PHI leaves the VPC in plaintext and wants a short list of telemetry categories that might be sent outside the VPC (e.g., failure counters, anonymized metrics). We also need retention windows for those items.

3) Subprocessors & geofencing — procurement needs to know the current subprocessors that may touch telemetry or logs, and whether you can commit to geofencing (US-only) for those subprocessors in the initial contract term.

I'll attach our preliminary DPA questions and the deployment topology for context. Can you provide a written summary we can attach to the RFP? If possible, please include sample evidence we can show our auditors (runbook excerpts, diagrams, or attestations).

Attachments: Catalyst_DPA_Questions_20271201.pdf, prod-topology.png

Appreciate a response this week if we want to keep to our timeline.

— Alex
Alex Jensen
Head of Cloud Security, Catalyst Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Customer keys & egress authorization for private deployment

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. High level answers below; Rachel and Irene are looped in for legal/ops detail and evidence. I will follow up with a short package (runbook excerpts + telemetry matrix) you can include in the RFP.

1) Key custody (BYOK)
- Yes: Redwood Private supports customer-managed CMKs. Customers can import/provision a key in their KMS/HSM and bind it to the Private control plane.
- Operator access: Redwood operators do NOT have access to plaintext customer keys. The platform uses envelope encryption; Redwood holds an operational key that is orthogonal to customer CMKs.
- Break-glass: Operator break-glass requires a documented emergency request, signed approval from the customer security contact, and a time-limited session recorded with immutable audit logs (KMS audit entries + platform telemetry). We can provide the template for the authorization form used in emergency unsealing.

2) Egress & telemetry
- We do not send customer data or inference payloads outside the VPC. Telemetry sent from the private control plane is limited to: health pings (aggregated), job failure counts (no request/response payloads), and anonymized capacity metrics.
- Retention: default telemetry retention is 30 days; we can negotiate shorter windows for enterprise contracts.

3) Subprocessors & geofencing
- Current subprocessors that may process telemetry metadata: Sentry (error aggregation, us-region), Datadog (metrics, us-region). Both are engaged only for optional, configurable exports — default installation does not enable them unless customer opts in.
- Geofencing: for Private deployments we can contractually restrict subprocessors to US-hosting for the initial term; Rachel can confirm language.

I'll attach an ops playbook snippet and our suggested DPA language for the key custody clause. Proposed next step: a short legal + ops call where we can walk through the runbook excerpts and the redlines.

Attachments: redwood_private_key_ops_playbook.pdf, byok-egress-matrix.csv

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Customer keys & egress authorization for private deployment

Alex / Marissa — quick legal note after reviewing Marissa's summary and Catalyst's attachment. Below are the items Legal wants reflected in the DPA redline and the evidence pack we can provide ahead of signature.

DPA redline requests (suggested):
- Section on Key Custody: Add language that (a) the customer retains sole control of CMKs for encryption of customer data; (b) Redwood will not access plaintext customer data or keys except under mutually agreed emergency procedures that require customer authorization; and (c) Redwood will maintain immutable audit logs for any operator actions affecting key material.
- Escrow/Recovery carveout: If Catalyst requires a key escrow mechanism for disaster recovery, we propose a separate Escrow Addendum outlining process, minimal prerequisites, and notarized custody.
- Subprocessors: Add a geofencing SLA for subprocessors touching telemetry metadata (US-only) and a 30-day notice before onboarding a new subprocessor.

Evidence pack we can provide (pre-signature):
- Runbook excerpt describing break-glass flow and audit trail (redwood_private_key_ops_playbook.pdf)
- Telemetry export matrix showing categories, fields withheld, and retention (byok-egress-matrix.csv)
- Example KMS audit log snippet (sanitized) — submit upon NDA if required
- Attestation: We can provide a short signed attestation of operator access controls after a successful security questionnaire. DocuSign link below to accept the standard attestation form.

Link: https://docusign.example.com/ABC-123-REDWOOD

I attached a redline we drafted (redline_dpa_v1.docx). Suggest we run a 30-minute session with Catalyst Legal to walk redlines and confirm the escrow options.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rachel — that is helpful. A couple of clarifying procurement/security questions before we lock the redline: 

- Export controls: does Redwood have any contractual or technical obligations that could require transfer of telemetry metadata to non-US jurisdictions (e.g., to support global support teams)? If so, we need a commitment that telemetries for Catalyst will be stored and processed only in the US for the initial contract term.

- Evidence: procurement requests a formal timeline for the sanitized KMS audit snippet and the attestation. Can you confirm when we can expect those artifacts? (We'd like to present them at our internal compliance review on 12/10.)

- Subprocessor exceptions: if Redwood must rely on a non-US subprocessor for an operational emergency, what is the emergency definition and notification cadence to Catalyst? We need this spelled out to satisfy our legal/compliance team.

I attached a short procurement checklist for your reference.

— Alex
Alex Jensen
Head of Cloud Security, Catalyst Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@catalysthealth.com>

Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2027 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Customer keys & egress authorization for private deployment

Alex — thanks for the pinpointed questions. Quick answers and proposed cadence so Procurement can close the packet: 

- Export controls / geofencing: Redwood will commit to US-only processing and storage of telemetry metadata for the initial 12-month contract term. This will be reflected in the DPA as a Subprocessor Geofence SLA (US-only) with a 30-day notice period for any exception.

- Evidence timeline: we will provide the sanitized KMS audit snippet and the signed attestation by 2027-12-09 (to meet your 12/10 internal review). Rachel will send the DocuSign attestation by end of day tomorrow.

- Emergency exceptions for non-US subprocessors: definition of emergency = catastrophic service degradation for >6 hours impacting production where no US-hosted remediation path exists. In such a case Redwood will: (1) notify Catalyst within 1 hour of decision to engage a non-US subprocessor; (2) limit data scope to minimal metadata required for remediation; (3) provide a post-incident report and audit logs within 72 hours. We will include this flow in the Escalation Addendum.

Next steps I suggest:
- Rachel to circulate DPA redline (done) and DocuSign attestation (in progress)
- Ops (Irene) to deliver the sanitized KMS audit snippet and the runbook excerpt by 2027-12-09
- 30-minute sync between Catalyst Legal/Procurement and Redwood Legal/Ops — propose Tue 2027-12-07 or Wed 2027-12-08 (use my calendar link).

Attachments: compliance-binder-snapshot.zip

Looking forward to the call — we'll be prepared with the evidence pack.

Best,
Marissa Cole
